A farm dog lies flat out and fully committed in the one patch of bale-shadow, stretched long against the twine with one ear turned inside out.
A tabby barn cat sits small on the very top of the heaped load, upright and entirely unbothered, tail curled round its own feet.
A heavy-footed horse stands in harness at the wagon shaft, head right down in the bristle, working steadily through anything worth eating.
A scatter of sparrows works the cut floor small and busy just behind the combed ridge, hopping and flicking broken stalks over.
A brown hare sits up small at the edge of the tall uncut grass, ears laid flat back, entirely unbothered by any of it.
Six swallows cut low and fast across the open cut ground, small and dark, turning hard at the hedge and coming straight back.
A grey donkey stands small beside the field gate with a tin can hung by its wire handle on the post above its ears, dozing exactly where it was left.
A black-and-white sheepdog sits bolt upright and small on top of a bale, surveying the whole field with the air of being in charge of it.
Two brown hens work the loose hay at the foot of the stack, small and low, turning it over stalk by stalk with real method.
Two jackdaws work the top bar of the field gate, small and busy, one of them dragging a length of loose twine about.
A ginger farm cat lies small and boneless along the flat top of the dry-stone wall, one paw hanging off the edge.
A kestrel hangs dead still and small high over the cut ground, wings going hard, holding one single spot in the air.
A soft-eyed brown cow stands small at the far side of the cut with her head over the fence rail, watching the whole business closely.
A litter of half-grown kittens tumbles small in a soft heap of loose hay at the foot of the stack, one of them buried to the ears.
